name: Joint pair decoding with a NEGATIVE_OTHER gate (argmax over reversal-consistent label pairs)
links: Task scorer (evaluation_functions/metrics.py in github.com/ilopezgazpio/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI): a reversible pair is soft-consistent only if first_prediction is in {EQ, FE, BE} and second_prediction == Rev(first_prediction); HardCons requires both rows correct. Related prior art: Mitchell et al. 2022 ConCoRD 'Enhancing Self-Consistency and Performance of Pre-Trained Language Models through NLI' (EMNLP, arXiv:2211.11875; weighted MaxSAT over model beliefs at inference time); Li et al. 2019 'A Logic-Driven Framework for Consistency of Neural Models' (EMNLP, arXiv:1909.00126); Wang et al. 2019 'What if we simply swap the two text fragments?' (AAAI; premise/hypothesis swap for NLI); Kassner et al. 2021 BeliefBank (EMNLP); test-time augmentation / product-of-experts pooling. In-repo anchor: src/labels.py (LABELS order EQ, FE, BE, NEG; REVERSE_PERM = (0, 2, 1, 3); reverse_instance_id).
year: Constrained / consistency-aware inference has roots in 2019-2022 NLP work; this specific formulation is proposed for DiCo-NLI (2026)
license_access: Method only; no license constraints. Works with any model that outputs per-class scores (open-weight or API).
track_coverage: All four tracks (T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed). Language-agnostic: only requires locating each row's reversed twin, whose id is deterministic (<pair_id>__<l1>-<l2>__original <-> <pair_id>__<l2>-<l1>__flipped). In T4 the twin of an en-es row is the es-en row, so it composes naturally with cross-lingual view aggregation over the same pair_id.
basque_quality: Not applicable (post-processing). It inherits the Basque quality of the underlying classifier; if anything it helps more on T3/T4 because weaker models are less order-consistent, so there is more inconsistency to repair.
cross_lingual_robustness: Neutral to positive. In T4 the two ordered rows of a pair are in different language orders (en-eu vs eu-en), so combining them averages over language-order effects. Extending the product to all views of the same pair_id (monolingual and mixed, mapped to the canonical 'original' frame with REVERSE_PERM for flipped rows) further removes language-specific noise.
architecture: Inference-time decoding. For twin rows x = (a, b) and x_rev = (b, a) with calibrated log-probabilities l = log p(.|a,b) and l_rev = log p(.|b,a): score each consistent joint assignment y in {EQ, FE, BE} as S(y) = l[y] + l_rev[Rev(y)] (equivalently pool l with l_rev[REVERSE_PERM]); optionally score the NEG option S(NEG) = l[NEG] + l_rev[NEG] + beta. Gate variants: (1) soft gate: include NEG in the argmax with a tuned bias beta; (2) hard gate: predict NEG for both rows if the pooled NEG probability exceeds a threshold tau, else argmax over {EQ, FE, BE}; (3) twin-aware gate: rows that have a twin never receive NEG (tau = 1), singletons use row-level argmax with their own NEG threshold. Output x -> y*, x_rev -> Rev(y*). Pooling can use log-prob sum (product of experts) or prob average; with multiple models or views, sum log-probs over all members before the argmax. Complexity is trivial (4 candidates per pair).
params: 0 learned parameters; 1-3 tuned scalars (NEG bias beta or threshold tau per track, optional softmax temperature per model).
compute: Negligible: a vectorised numpy/pandas operation over the prediction table; runs on CPU in milliseconds. Requires two forward passes per source pair, which the data already provides (both orders are separate rows).
sample_efficiency: Very sample-efficient: only 1-3 scalars are tuned, on grouped-CV out-of-fold predictions (train has ~1,282 reversible pairs and 478 NEG singletons per monolingual track; dev has 277 pairs + 106 NEG). Reduces seed variance of consistency metrics because SoftCons becomes deterministic (1.0 on non-NEG-predicted pairs) and HardCons becomes pair accuracy of a pooled (two-view) predictor, which is smoother than per-row predictions.
reported_results: No published DiCo-NLI numbers. Analytical results from the official scorer: (1) SoftCons = fraction of gold-reversible pairs whose joint prediction is not NEG, so with the twin-aware gate SoftCons = 1.0 exactly; (2) HardCons = accuracy of the joint label over reversible pairs (both rows correct iff the joint label is correct); (3) Weighted F1 changes by the net effect of pooling two views (typically a small gain, like test-time augmentation). Reference gaps showing the headroom: in the LREC 2026 pilot, the best models had unseen SoftCoh 0.80-0.84 and HardCoh 0.72-0.79 (DeBERTa-v3-B 0.84/0.79, BART-L 0.80/0.72, OPT-125M 0.65/0.58), i.e. 16-35% of pairs were order-inconsistent, all of which joint decoding makes consistent. Analogous inference-time consistency correction (ConCoRD) improved accuracy of QA/VQA models by several points while raising consistency [uncertain on transfer]. Expected on DiCo: SoftCons 0.84 -> 1.00, HardCons +3-8 points, Weighted F1 +0-2 points [uncertain].
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the pilot; the pilot only measured raw per-row predictions (encoders SoftCoh up to 0.85 unseen, HardCoh up to 0.79). Those inconsistency rates quantify the SoftCons headroom this method closes.
consistency_guarantee: inference-time (decoding): guarantees Rev-consistency for every pair decoded jointly; SoftCons = 1.0 on all gold-reversible pairs whose joint prediction is not NEG (exactly 1.0 with the twin-aware gate).
negative_other_handling: Decided at pair level: either both rows NEG or neither. With a soft/hard gate it can still emit NEG on gold-reversible pairs (both rows NEG gives soft_ok = False in the scorer because NEG is not in REVERSIBLE_LABELS, and HardCons = 0), so the gate threshold should be tuned for the combined objective. In train/dev every twin-bearing row is gold-reversible and every NEGATIVE_OTHER row is a singleton, so on data built the same way the optimal gate is 'never NEG on twins' (the structural cue); a rule-safe variant tunes tau on grouped-CV without using the singleton cue, keeping NEG possible on twins when evidence is very strong. Singletons are decoded row-wise (4-way argmax with a tuned NEG bias).
metric_tradeoff: SoftCons: large gain, up to 1.0. HardCons: gain equal to converting half-correct/inconsistent pairs into jointly-correct ones when the pooled evidence favours the right label; never limited by inconsistency any more, only by pair accuracy. Weighted F1: small gain on average (two-view pooling), but can lose on pairs where one row was right and the pooled decision picks the other row's wrong label (those pairs had HardCons = 0 anyway). Gate trade-off: a lower NEG threshold raises NEG recall (F1 on the ~16% NEG class) but costs SoftCons/HardCons on reversible pairs; a higher threshold does the opposite.
integration: Pure post-processing step after any model: (1) collect per-row 4-way log-probs in LABELS order (src/labels.py); (2) map each row to its twin with reverse_instance_id and group rows by pair; (3) compute pooled scores l + l_rev[REVERSE_PERM], apply the gate, write labels for both rows; singletons fall back to row-level argmax. Implement as e.g. src/pipelines/decode.py with a function joint_decode(df, logprobs, tau, beta) and a CLI flag in the prediction script; tune tau/beta on out-of-fold grouped-CV predictions. Composes with view aggregation (sum over all views of the pair_id in the canonical frame) and with model ensembling (sum member log-probs first).
ensemble_compatibility: Yes, it is the consumer of calibrated probabilities: works best with temperature-scaled per-class probabilities; ensembles are combined by summing log-probs before the joint argmax. Hard-label-only members (e.g. API LLM without logprobs) can be added as smoothed one-hot or vote-frequency distributions.
inference_cost: Zero beyond base model inference; decoding all tracks (~6k rows) takes milliseconds on CPU.
rules_disclosure: Post-processing using the test set's own inputs (pairing a row with its reversed twin) is transductive inference at test time; it should be disclosed in the system paper as consistency-aware joint decoding. The twin-aware gate additionally exploits dataset construction (twins are reversible, NEG items are singletons), which is a structural cue: it is exact on train/dev but should be disclosed explicitly and may be judged as exploiting an artefact; final rules could forbid using instance_id structure or cross-instance information [uncertain]. The generic version (twins found by swapping text1/text2 and a learned NEG gate) is robust to renamed ids.
contamination: None (uses no external data; operates only on model outputs).
structural_cue_dependence: Moderate. Needs twin identification: via instance_id convention or, more robustly, by matching rows whose (text1, text2) are swapped within the test file. The 'never NEG on twins' gate depends on the singleton-NEG construction; if the test file contains NEG items with twins or unpaired reversible items, fall back to the tuned tau/beta gate, which degrades gracefully to ordinary two-view pooling.
expected_gain: Highest expected gain per unit effort: SoftCons jumps to ~1.0 (from ~0.80-0.85 for the pilot's best models), HardCons rises by several points (every previously inconsistent-but-half-right pair gets a chance to become fully right, and pooled two-view evidence is more accurate), and Weighted F1 is typically flat to slightly up. It is model-agnostic, zero-training, and a prerequisite component for ensembling and cross-lingual view aggregation, so it should be implemented first and applied to every submission; the only decision is how aggressively to use the twin => not-NEG structural cue, which should be settled against the final rules.
